# LLM evals

Use when changing prompts, models, tools or retrieval for an LLM feature.

## Build the dataset
1. Collect 50–200 real inputs, including the edge cases and failures users reported.
2. For each, write what a good answer must contain or must not do. Exact strings are rarely the right target.
3. Keep a held-out slice you never tune against.

## Choose graders
- Code checks first: JSON validity, schema, required fields, length, forbidden content, tool-call arguments.
- Reference comparisons for factual answers.
- Model-graded rubrics for tone or helpfulness. Calibrate the grader against human labels on a sample, and read disagreements.

## Run
- Fix model, temperature and seed where possible, and run each case several times when outputs vary.
- Record cost and latency with the scores. A better answer at five times the cost may not be better.

## Gate
- Compare against the current production version, not an absolute bar.
- Block a release on statistically clear regressions in must-pass cases. Review every case that flipped from pass to fail.
- Add every new production failure to the dataset.

## Verify
Show the before/after table (score, pass rate, cost, latency) and links to the flipped cases.
